claims.text: Standard SLM-produced high-entropy-alloy components typically exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
Standard SLM-produced high-entropy-alloy components typically contain residual thermal stresses.
Standard SLM-produced high-entropy-alloy components typically contain porosity and microstructural defects.
An in-situ laser-remelting pass after every SLM layer will improve dimensional precision.
An in-situ laser-remelting pass after every SLM layer will improve mechanical integrity.
Layer-wise laser remelting will reduce residual stresses.
Layer-wise laser remelting will reduce porosity.
Layer-wise laser remelting will reduce microstructural inhomogeneities.
The remelting pass will produce a more uniform grain structure.
Reduced porosity, mitigated residual stress, and a more uniform grain structure will improve interlayer bonding.
The additional laser-remelting pass lowers local thermal gradients.
The additional pass causes partial remelting and homogenization of the alloy.
Lower thermal gradients and remelting-driven homogenization reduce microvoid formation and residual stress.
Remelting-driven microstructural refinement enhances dimensional fidelity.
Relative to standard SLM, layer-wise remelting is expected to reduce dimensional deviation by approximately 5% or more.
Relative to standard SLM, layer-wise remelting is expected to improve yield strength and fracture toughness by approximately 10–20%.
The predicted benefit should hold for high-entropy alloys processed by laser powder-bed fusion under conventional geometries and laser parameters.
The predicted benefit may not hold when rapid scanning or extreme energy densities dominate the build.
The predicted benefit may not transfer to non-laser additive-manufacturing methods.
Additional laser passes may introduce new defects.
